proof:
# Concavity and zero boundary values do not imply the proposed capacity bound

This is an exact counterexample to the general functional capacity statement.
It is not a counterexample when the function is required to be the actual
own-fiber halfspace-depth root. That narrower property has additional
structure not used by the disproved formulation.

For a finite base P and nonnegative function g on a convex domain D, write

    A_z=max_(x in D_z) g(z,x),
    nu(H)=sum_(z in P) sup_(x in D_z, (z,x) in H) g(z,x),

where an empty supremum contributes zero. The proposed exponent-one claim
would give a point whose every containing halfspace has capacity at least
(sum_z A_z)/h(P).

## Exact planar construction

Take P={0,1,2}, whose finite-base Helly number is two. Define

    u(z)=min(z,2-z)+1/10,
    D={(z,x):0<=z<=2, 0<=x<=u(z)},
    g(z,x)=min(3-z+(3/2)x, 1000x, 1000(u(z)-x)).           (1)

The domain is a convex body. The function is nonnegative, continuous and
jointly concave, because it is the minimum of finitely many affine functions
on D. It is positive in the relative interior of every specified continuous
fiber and zero at both endpoints of that fiber. Thus every specified fiber
is a positive-length interval and the zero-boundary condition is satisfied.

Put q=2000/2003. The peak values and their points are exactly

    A_0=6300/2003,      x_0=194/2003,
    A_1=7300/2003,      x_1=2196/2003,
    A_2=2300/2003,      x_2=198/2003.                     (2)

Indeed the increasing affine roof and the decreasing right-end tent meet at

    x_z=[1000u(z)-(3-z)]/(1000+3/2),

with value q[3-z+(3/2)u(z)]. At each displayed point the left-end term
1000x_z is strictly larger. Both branches are monotone in opposite
directions, proving these are the global maxima of (1) on the fibers.

Their total peak mass is 15900/2003, so the claimed capacity threshold is

    (sum A_z)/2=7950/2003.                               (3)

## Every candidate has a strictly smaller cap

For a point in the fiber z=0, the cap z<=0 has capacity A_0. For a point in
the fiber z=2, the cap z>=2 has capacity A_2.

Now take a point (1,x) in the middle fiber. If x>1/10, the closed cap
x'>=x misses both endpoint fibers and has capacity at most A_1.
If 0<=x<=1/10, use the closed oblique cap

    H_x={(z',x'):x'<=10(z'-1)+x}.

It contains (1,x), excludes the entire left fiber, includes the entire
right fiber, and intersects the middle fiber only where x'<=x. There the
affine roof in (1) is at most 2+(3/2)(1/10)=43/20. Consequently

    nu(H_x)<=43/20+2300/2003 <7300/2003=A_1,              (4)

the last gap being 13871/40060>0.

Thus every point has a containing closed ambient halfspace of capacity at
most A_1. Conversely, at the middle peak any containing halfspace has
capacity at least that peak value A_1 from its own fiber. Therefore the
maximum capacity depth is EXACTLY

    max_(y in D intersect (P times R)) inf_(H contains y) nu(H)
       =7300/2003 <7950/2003.                            (5)

The exact deficit is 650/2003. Joint piecewise-linear concavity, bounded
convex support, full-dimensional positive fibers, and vanishing fiber
boundary values all hold. None rescues the general capacity claim.

## A separate exponent-two affine example

The fiber-functional agent independently found a simpler example for
the squared capacity before the zero-boundary strengthening above. Let

    D={(z,x,y):0<=z<=2, -1/10<=x<=min(z,2-z)+1/10,
                              -1<=y<=1},
    g(z,x,y)=2-z/2+x/2,
    A_z=max_(D_z) g(z,x,y)^2.

This is a positive affine function on a convex body, with full-dimensional
two-dimensional fibers. Its squared peaks are

    A_0=A_1=1681/400,     A_2=441/400.

The same vertical endpoint cuts and horizontal middle cuts x'>=x for
x>1/10 give capacities at most A_1. For middle x<=1/10, the oblique cut
x'<=10(z'-1)+x has capacity at most

    (31/20)^2+(21/20)^2=1402/400 <A_1.

The maximum squared-capacity depth is therefore exactly 1681/400, below
the proposed half total 3803/800 by 441/800. This version does not vanish
on the fiber boundaries; the preceding exponent-one example shows that
zero boundary values alone are not the missing structural condition.

Exact peak and cap arithmetic is checked in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_concave_fiber_capacity_counterexample.py`.
